Authority converges for issue #17. This is construction authority only; it authorizes later Plan/Apply work and is not implementation proof.

Evidence basis: the sealed issue statement is corroborated by the current implementation and durable refusals. `src/reviewer-role.ts` exposes arbitrary per-leg prompt strings and calls `runAgent` immediately after the first leg’s ledger admission; it has no all-legs construction gate. `src/reviewer-execution-ledger.ts` and `src/reviewer-auditor.ts` already preserve the actual attempted prompts and send them, the canonical Skill, task, child reports, batch provenance, and candidate Receipt to the post-run audit. `.ak/dockets/issues/15/review/review-001/result/receipt.json`, `review-002/result/receipt.json`, and `review-003/result/receipt.json` establish the over-broad command, impossible free-text allowlist, and abbreviated Fowler-baseline failures after the sole batch had run. The canonical external `code-review` Skill requires the complete baseline, fixed range, separate Standards/Spec burdens, parallel dispatch, and separate aggregation.

## Clause disposition

A1–A6 are accepted. They govern every proposed two-leg Standards/Spec dispatch. The canonical no-spec path remains a prerequisite/skip path: an explicitly established “no spec available” state creates no Spec prompt and consumes no two-leg batch. It must not be represented as a malformed or one-legged batch.

## Boundary decisions

**U1 — Interface seam: one atomic two-leg construction/dispatch seam.** Replace the parent-visible arbitrary per-leg prompt dispatch surface for this method with one atomic Standards/Spec proposal. The proposal contains structured review declarations, not child prompt prose. The Reviewer runtime owns compilation and validates both complete legs before the dispatcher may create a workspace, invoke a provider, or mark either child started. One accepted atomic call starts the two isolated legs as one sibling-parallel batch. A rejected proposal is an ordinary preflight rejection, not infrastructure failure and not a batch. This internal two-leg seam is not role topology and does not alter caller-owned role ordering or repetition.

**U2 — Compilation ownership: deterministic construction, semantic sufficiency retained by the existing audit.** Runtime-owned deterministic construction must bind: (1) the exact canonical Skill snapshot; (2) the exact opaque task identity; (3) resolved base, target, range/diff command, and commit list; (4) exact identified material bytes and identities; (5) the complete canonical Standards baseline and fixed axis briefs; and (6) the per-leg capability declaration. Standards receives only the common target/provenance block, standards materials, complete baseline, and Standards burden. Spec receives only the common target/provenance block, spec materials, and Spec burden. There is no model-authored free-text instruction slot through which requirements can be abbreviated or blended.

Preflight mechanically rejects incomplete canonical sections, wrong or duplicate axes, cross-axis material placement, missing identities/bytes, range inconsistency, capability inconsistency, and any output not reproduced exactly by the selected construction recipe. It is deterministic and uses no model. The post-run compliance audit remains the sole semantic method auditor: it decides whether the selected sources were semantically sufficient, resolves genuinely ambiguous material classification, verifies actual dispatch identity and fixed-target traceability from runtime evidence, checks successful child evidence and axis isolation, and checks faithful separate aggregation. It does not redo the substantive review. Thus C4 is addressed by eliminating arbitrary prompt prose and enforcing axis-owned compartments, not by a nonblank/digest-only check; irreducible source sufficiency is deliberately left to the existing audit under A4.

**U3 — Executable policy: structured least-privilege capabilities are the exclusive executable authority.** Executable restrictions must not be inferred from or imposed by opaque task prose. Caller-authorized capabilities are supplied as structured input and bound to the task identity; the Reviewer proposal declares the exact capabilities each leg needs. The effective grant is the declared set only, and preflight requires it to be a subset of both caller authorization and host availability. Canonical prerequisite operations and every declared verification operation must be satisfiable before dispatch. A missing requirement rejects both legs before start; the runtime must never repair it by widening access. Child execution is mechanically confined to the accepted grant, and undeclared operations remain unavailable. Legacy free-text “only run …” language has no independent executable-policy force and must not be copied wholesale into child prompts; callers that intend such a restriction must express it in the structured policy. This resolves C2 without granting broad shell access.

**U4 — Correction law: correction is allowed before the sole accepted dispatch; the bound is lifecycle, not a numeric retry count.** After a typed preflight rejection, the parent may submit a corrected structured proposal in the same invocation. Corrections cease permanently when the atomic dispatcher records the accepted dispatch-start transition; no correction or second batch is then legal. There is no package-owned numeric attempt cap: ADR 0007 rejects fixed retry brakes absent failure evidence, and ADR 0010 leaves invocation budget/abort policy to the caller. The invocation/caller abort boundary is the budget bound.

The construction ledger must monotonically record each proposal identity and preflight disposition. A rejection proves no child started by containing no dispatch-start transition, child start identity, workspace creation, provider invocation, or child usage; the dispatcher owning all child starts must make those states unrepresentable before acceptance. Rejected proposal records are minimal structured evidence, not retained generic session/tool-event payloads.

**U5 — Evidence identity: retain the exact compiled prompts.** For the accepted batch, durable Reviewer method evidence retains each exact compiled prompt byte sequence, byte length, and SHA-256, together with the exact canonical Skill/task/range/material/capability identities and construction-recipe version. Dispatch must use those immutable bytes without a later prompt transformation; the dispatch seam records the actual prompt identity/SHA, while the existing execution record continues to give the audit the exact actual prompt. This permits direct byte/hash equality proof without retaining a generic session transcript or generic tool-event payload. Rejected proposals retain only their structured identity, digest, violations, and no-start lifecycle evidence unless compilation produced exact candidate prompts needed to explain the rejection.

## Counterexample closure

- C1: the complete canonical baseline is runtime-owned construction, so abbreviation cannot reach a child.
- C2: an unsatisfied structured capability set rejects before dispatch and cannot auto-widen.
- C3: the atomic owner cannot start either leg before both pass.
- C4: arbitrary axis prose is removed and typed material compartments are validated; remaining semantic source sufficiency stays with the post-run audit.
- C5: preflight is deterministic and non-model-based.

## Scope/Soul

The current Reviewer Soul already contains only the irreducible judgment kernel and remains unchanged. Fowler text, prompt templates, fields, CLI/transport mechanics, lifecycle counts, and task policy belong in the canonical Skill, schema/runtime, documentation, or host input—not Soul. Existing post-run audit authority, exactly-one started sibling-batch law, active-model behavior, role boundaries, caller-owned orchestration, and the reserved cross-model-panel concept remain unchanged.
